intro: Requires Solo ambient, the agentgateway waypoint controller and the petshop Keycloak realm on mesh1. This lab deploys its own application. It shares petshop with the Ambient L4 identity lab; reset that lab before starting this one.

3.1.title: Deploy petshop and its waypoint
3.1.say: Deploy the application, create a waypoint and enrol petshop's Services.
3.1.point: The waypoint's own log: every request now carries the caller's SPIFFE identity, method, path and status.

blocks.title: Deploy petshop, add the waypoint

parts.title: Enrol the namespace
parts.instruction: Create the petshop namespace with ambient enabled.
parts.expect: The namespace is created or configured.

parts.title: Deploy petshop
parts.instruction: Apply the API and client deployments. Wait for them to become ready and remove earlier identity policies.
parts.expect: All five application deployments are ready.

parts.title: Create and attach the waypoint
parts.instruction: Create a Gateway using the enterprise-agentgateway-waypoint class and label the namespace to use it.
parts.expect: petshop-waypoint is ready and the namespace is labelled.

parts.title: Check the waypoint log
parts.instruction: Read recent requests handled by the waypoint.
parts.expect: The access log includes a successful request, its method, path and workload identity.

blocks.show:
kind: Gateway
  gatewayClassName: enterprise-agentgateway-waypoint
kubectl label ns petshop \
  istio.io/use-waypoint=petshop-waypoint

3.2.title: Authorise requests using JWT claims
3.2.say: Require a Keycloak token. Permit authenticated reads and restrict deletion to admins.
3.2.point: Authentication failures return 401. A valid user without permission receives 403.

blocks.title: Look inside bob's token
blocks.instruction: Request a token from Keycloak and decode its issuer, username and roles.
blocks.expect: The token is issued by the petshop realm and bob has the admin role.
blocks.show:
curl -d grant_type=password -d username=bob ... $KEYCLOAK/token
# decode the payload: iss, user, realm roles

blocks.title: JWT and authorisation on the waypoint
blocks.instruction: Attach strict JWT authentication and method-based authorisation to the waypoint.
blocks.expect: Both policies are Accepted and Attached.
blocks.show:
# petshop-jwt
jwtAuthentication: { mode: Strict }
# petshop-authz
authorization: CEL over the JWT claims

blocks.title: Test user permissions
blocks.instruction: Compare anonymous requests with reads and deletes made by alice and bob.
blocks.expect: No token: 401. Alice can read but cannot delete. Bob can delete.
blocks.show:
GET    /pets     no token
GET    /pets     alice
DELETE /pets/1   alice (user)
DELETE /pets/1   bob (admin)

3.3.title: Route requests to a canary version
3.3.say: Send 10% of requests to v2. Use x-beta: true to select v2 explicitly.
3.3.point: Callers never change the URL they call. The split happens at the waypoint.

blocks.title: Deploy v2 and the route

parts.title: Deploy petstore-v2
parts.instruction: Deploy a second version with its own Service and the same workload identity.

parts.title: Apply the routing rules
parts.instruction: Attach an HTTPRoute to petstore. Set the default split to 90/10 and send the beta header to v2.
parts.expect: The route is accepted by Service/petstore.

blocks.show:
kind: HTTPRoute   # parent: Service/petstore
  x-beta: true -> petstore-v2
  otherwise    -> v1 90 / v2 10

blocks.title: Send traffic
blocks.instruction: Measure 20 ordinary requests and five beta requests, then try a request without a token.
blocks.expect: The weighted sample varies. All beta requests reach v2, and the anonymous request returns 401.
blocks.show:
20 x GET  with alice's token
 5 x GET  with x-beta: true
 1 x GET  with no token

3.4.title: Limit requests by workload identity
3.4.say: Limit storefront to five requests per minute and compare it with checkout using the same user token.
3.4.point: storefront gets five then 429. checkout-blue, same alice token, gets all eight.

blocks.title: Limit storefront, call from both

parts.title: Apply the storefront limit
parts.instruction: Attach a conditional rate limit matching the storefront ServiceAccount.
parts.expect: The policy is applied. Other ServiceAccounts are not included.

parts.title: Compare the two workloads
parts.instruction: Get alice's token and send eight requests from each workload.
parts.expect: storefront is rate-limited. checkout-blue's requests return 200.

blocks.show:
rateLimit:
  conditional:
  - condition: 'source.identity.serviceAccount == "storefront"'
    policy: { local: [{ requests: 5, unit: Minutes }] }

3.5.title: Forward the verified username
3.5.say: Set request and response headers from the verified JWT username.
3.5.point: The response header proves the response transformation ran. The request transformation is configured to set x-user for the backend.

blocks.title: Set a header from the verified claim

parts.title: Apply the header transformation
parts.instruction: Remove the previous rate limit and set x-user and x-authenticated-user from the verified username.

parts.title: Inspect the response headers
parts.instruction: Request petstore as alice and inspect the status and identity header.

blocks.show:
transformation:
  request:  set x-user: jwt.preferred_username
  response: set x-authenticated-user: jwt.preferred_username

checks.label: Identity header set by the gateway

3.6.title: External authorisation options
3.6.say: Review where an external authorisation service can replace the inline policy decision.
3.6.point: This chapter is reference material. It does not deploy or test an external authorisation service.
3.6.notes: An external authorisation service can use data that is not present in the request, such as account status or centrally managed permissions. OPA can evaluate those rules. The waypoint calls the service and uses its allow or deny decision. Plan how to handle timeouts and service outages before using this in an application.
